subject: Animation
title: The Multiplane Camera
description: Learn The Multiplane Camera in one minute.

hook.text: In the 1930s, Disney built a camera that shot through stacked layers of painted glass.

buildup.text: Each glass layer held a different part of the scene — foreground, midground, and background.

discovery.text: By moving the layers at different speeds, the camera created a stunning illusion of depth.

twist.text: The device was enormous and expensive. Some shots took hours to set up for seconds of film.

climax.text: The multiplane camera debuted in The Old Mill and became essential to Disney's visual style.

punchline.text: Stacked glass gave flat drawings a third dimension.

quiz.question: What did Disney's multiplane camera achieve?
options: It added synchronized sound to cartoons
It created an illusion of depth by photographing through stacked painted glass layers
It allowed animators to draw directly onto film
